reader.requirement: At --std 85, the LINE-COUNTER and PAGE-COUNTER of a report whose RD carries GLOBAL must be global names: referenceable (qualified by the report-name, or unqualified where it is the only such counter the program has) from every program directly or indirectly contained in the declaring program, naming the same registers the declaring program sees; the counters of a non-GLOBAL report must not be reachable from a containee.
reader.edition-search: read ReportOf, InheritGlobalReport, InheritContainerReports and the GLOBAL arm of BindReportDescriptionClauses; grep of Edition.Has/Edition.Edition/DialectLevel/CobolVersion/DialectBehavior/ConstructRegistry over ReportSectionBinder.cs and CounterResolver.cs: the only DialectLevel use in ReportSectionBinder is the CONTROL-operand uniqueness screen (SR6, not this rule), and ReportOf / NearestInScope consult no edition; no construct row gates the RD GLOBAL clause.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a direct containee reading both counters (qualified and unqualified) of a GLOBAL report; not exercised: indirect containment, a containee with its own report beside the inherited one (nearest-element qualification), a containee altering PAGE-COUNTER OF the global report, and the refusal for a non-GLOBAL report. All probed here.

probes.printed: M LC=03 / D OWN LC=10 / D R-1 LC=03 / D R-1 LC=05 / M LC=05 / M PC=07
probes.expected: indirectly contained D: unqualified LINE-COUNTER is its own R-3's (10, FIRST DETAIL 10); LINE-COUNTER OF/IN R-1 is the container's (3, then 5 after D's two GENERATEs of the global detail); MOVE 7 TO PAGE-COUNTER OF R-1 (§1985:XIII.3.5.5 rule 6 allows procedure statements to alter it) is seen by the declaring program

probes.printed: error COBOL2729: LINE-COUNTER referenced, but the program has no report description entry; error COBOL2729: PAGE-COUNTER OF 'R-2': the qualifier shall name a report description entry
probes.expected: R-2 is not GLOBAL: its counters are not global names and the containee may not reference them

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR1  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: A GLOBAL RD is inherited into every containee through InheritedGlobals.Reports and ReportScope; ReportOf resolves the counter against the nearest declaring element's reports, so a containee's own report wins an unqualified reference and the inherited one answers its report-name qualifier. The counters are runtime registers of the one report instance, so reads and writes in the containee are the container's. No edition is consulted on this path.

refuter.evidence: rpa.cob (run rpa-001, --std 85): A has GLOBAL RD R-A and contains B; B has GLOBAL RD R-B and contains D; D has a non-GLOBAL RD R-D and contains E; E has no RD. E printed 'E UNQ LC=10 / E R-A LC=03': the unqualified counter skips D's non-GLOBAL R-D and resolves to the nearest GLOBAL one, R-B (LC 10 at its FIRST DETAIL), per X.1.3.8.2 GR1/GR3b, and OF R-A reaches the outermost one. D's own detail line 'SOURCE LINE-COUNTER OF R-A / OF R-B / unqualified' wrote '03 10 05' to RPAD.RPT: in the Report Section a global counter of a different report is reached by explicit report-name qualification (SRL2.9), and the unqualified one is implicitly R-D's. rpb.cob (rpb-001, compile only): a containee with no RD under a container with two GLOBAL RDs, unqualified LINE-COUNTER and PAGE-COUNTER, is refused with COBOL2729 twice. That is right: two objects are identified, neither local and both declared in the same program, so no rule of X.1.3.8.2 GR3 picks one. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR1 ... the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 ... it lies in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.9 ... the text is in SRL2.9'. Unlike LinageFileOf (previous case), ReportOf uses Reports.NearestInScope, so the multi-level arm is right.
